subject.title: [Bug]: openclaw status falsely reports openclaw-mem0 memory as unavailable when the live gateway plugin is working

question: Should memory status be resolved from live gateway runtime health, from a passive local plugin status contract, or should the current `not checked` mitigation be accepted as sufficient?
rationale: Current main avoids the old exact wording but does not satisfy the issue's requested live-runtime health contract, and the broader canonical issue plus open fork PR require an owner choice before automation should implement more behavior.

options.title: Use the broader live-gateway contract
options.body: Make https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/62599 the canonical implementation path, require live external-memory proof, and close or replace the fork PR after choosing the design.

options.title: Revive the fork PR
options.body: Ask the fork PR author to rebase and prove `status --deep` plus JSON output against a real external memory plugin without local plugin side effects.

options.title: Accept `not checked` as enough
options.body: Declare the current softened status output sufficient, close the fork PR, and close this issue with explicit maintainer rationale.

recommendation.title: Use the broader live-gateway contract
recommendation.body: Make https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/62599 the canonical implementation path, require live external-memory proof, and close or replace the fork PR after choosing the design.

likelyOwner.reason: The decision is about the memory plugin/status owner boundary that Peter's memory runtime and status refactors introduced and continue to shape.
